Sure! Running an Integrated Regression (IREG) for a bug fix typically follows a standard workflow. Below is a quick‑start guide you can adapt to your own build system or CI pipeline. If you let me know which product you’re targeting (e.g., `fc`, `starrc`, `pt`, or `nt`), I can tailor the commands more precisely. --- ## Quick‑Start Guide to Run IREG for a Bug Fix | Step | What to Do | Why it Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Checkout the Bug Branch** | `git checkout ` | Make sure you’re working on the branch that contains the bug‑fix changes. | | **2. Pull Latest Changes** | `git pull origin ` | Keeps your local copy up‑to‑date with any other work that may have been merged into the branch. | | **3. Set Up Environment Variables** | ```bash\nexport IREG_HOME=/opt/ireg\nexport PATH=$IREG_HOME/bin:$PATH\n``` | Points the shell to the IREG installation and ensures the `run_ireg` script is executable. | | **4. Clean Previous Builds** | `make clean` (or equivalent) | Removes stale artifacts so you start from a clean state. | | **5. Build the Design** | `make all` (or your build command) | Generates the netlist, timing constraints, and any other files required for IREG. | | **6. Run IREG** | `run_ireg --prod= --config=ireg.cfg` | Executes the IREG process for the specified product. Replace `` with `fc`, `starrc`, `pt`, or `nt`. | | **7. Review Results** | `open_report report.html` (or view the generated PDF) | Verify that the regression passed and that the bug is indeed fixed. | | **8. Commit & Push** | `git commit -am "Run IREG for bug #12345"`
`git push origin ` | Records the successful regression run in version control. | ### Example Command (Full Chip) If you’re targeting the Full Chip (`fc`) product, here’s a concrete example: ```bash # 1. Checkout the bug branch git checkout bug-12345-fix # 2. Pull latest changes git pull origin bug-12345-fix # 3. Set up environment export IREG_HOME=/opt/ireg export PATH=$IREG_HOME/bin:$PATH # 4. Clean previous builds make clean # 5. Build design make all # 6. Run IREG run_ireg --prod=fc --config=ireg.cfg # 7. Open results open_report report_fc_bug12345.html ``` ### Using the Integrated Function If you’d like me to invoke the `run_ireg` function directly (for example, in a scripted or automated context), just tell me the product code and any additional options you’d normally pass. Here’s how you would call it via the function interface: ```json { "name": "run_ireg", "arguments": { "prod": "fc" } } ``` Feel free to replace `"fc"` with `"starrc"`, `"pt"`, or `"nt"` depending on the target product. --- #### Common Pitfalls & Tips | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | “Command not found” when calling `run_ireg` | Ensure `$PATH` includes `$IREG_HOME/bin`. | | “Missing configuration file” | Verify that `ireg.cfg` exists in the current directory or supply its path with `--config=`. | | “Regression failed due to timing violations” | Check the detailed timing report; the bug might still be present or new issues were introduced. | | “Build fails before IREG runs” | Resolve compilation errors first; IREG requires a successful build to proceed. | Let me know if you need help customizing this for a particular build system (e.g., Ninja, SCons) or integrating it into your CI/CD pipeline. Happy debugging!
